From: Luca Bianchi <luca.bianchi@industria.it>

FW: I'm also joining — seeing the same. Calendly picked PST for me when I opened the link from Italy. I think Calendly uses browser locale or IP detection; if your account has an 'Event time zone' set that can help but not always.

A few workarounds we've used internally:
- Force timezone in the Calendly link via query param (Calendly supports ?timezone=Europe/Rome in some setups)
- Include explicit times in email + ask recipient to confirm and then send a manual calendar invite (preferred for cross-region demos)
- Create the event in Google Calendar in the organizer's timezone and then change event timezone before sending to guests (Google preserves timezone info in the .ics)

Luca
Head of ML Ops, Industria S.p.A.

Quick notes from ops:
- Calendly's timezone detection is usually fine, but browser settings and VPNs can override it. Also the DST mismatch (US 2nd Sun in Mar vs EU last Sun in Mar) can confuse people when scheduling a few weeks out.
- Workaround that consistently works: organizer sets the event timezone explicitly in Google Calendar before sending. Attach the .ics to the thread.
- Alternative: we can send a Chili Piper deep link that forces timezone and preferred rep: https://redwood.chilipiper.com/demo?tz=Europe%2FRome. Chili Piper tends to be more explicit about tz in the URL.

If Marissa wants, I can create the invite in Europe/Rome and include two .ics variants (Europe/Rome and America/Los_Angeles) so recipients can import the one that maps to their client. That sounds like overkill but it's robust.

–Jordan
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
